title: AttnDiff: Attention-based Differential Fingerprinting for Large Language Models
claim: Released models get laundered into suspect models of unknown origin; our fingerprint comparison against references reveals their lineage.
layout: 4 panels: three top stages left-to-right, wide bottom panel; detective mascot centered
description: The figure has four dashed, pastel-colored panels. The top row has three numbered stages running left to right. Stage 1, 'Released models', shows logos for Llama, Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Others. Stage 2, 'Model laundering', shows boxes for fine-tuning, pruning, merging, distillation, quantization and '...', linked by arrows. Stage 3, 'Suspect models', shows cartoon masked thieves carrying stamped 'STOLEN' bags, plus a '?' Unknown tile, under the question 'Whose model is it?'. A red arrow leads down to the wide bottom panel, 'AttnDiff investigates model provenance'. At the bottom, a large detective-with-magnifying-glass illustration labeled AttnDiff sits in the center. On its left are reference fingerprints for Llama, Qwen (highlighted) and GLM, drawn as purple striped bars. On its right is the suspect fingerprint bar, with arrows pointing toward the detective. The eye goes first to the detective and the thief icons.
caption: Model provenance verification with \attndiff. Top: publicly released checkpoints may undergo individual or composed transformations, resulting in suspect models whose origins are uncertain. Bottom: \attndiff{} independently extracts differential attention fingerprints from reference and suspect models using the same probe pairs, then compares them to assess evidence of shared lineage. Multiple references illustrate repeated pairwise comparisons. Model families, fingerprint patterns, and the highlighted match are illustrative.
abstract: Protecting the intellectual property of open-weight large language models (LLMs) requires verifying whether a suspect model is derived from a victim model despite common laundering operations such as fine-tuning (including PPO/DPO), pruning/compression, and model merging. We propose \textsc{AttnDiff}, a data-efficient white-box framework that extracts fingerprints from models via intrinsic information-routing behavior. \textsc{AttnDiff} probes minimally edited prompt pairs that induce controlled semantic conflicts, captures differential attention patterns, summarizes them with compact spectral descriptors, and compares models using CKA. Across Llama-2/3 and Qwen2.5 (3B--14B) and additional open-source families, it yields high similarity for related derivatives while separating unrelated model families (e.g., $>0.98$ vs.\ $<0.22$ with $M=60$ probes). With 5--60 multi-domain probes, it supports practical provenance verification and accountability.
